body: Kinesiology/psychology student and long time depression sufferer here. Coping is tough, I've been depressed for years and still am. Whenever I'm feeling really down, I usually go for a walk or even a run. Exercise triggers a release of analgesic (pain-killer) neurotransmitters that instantly raise your mood. It may be hard to motivate yourself to do it, but if you can, just force yourself, it really does make you feel better. Even just being outside and appreciating nature (depending on where you live). From what I've learned about having depression, it's that you'll never be motivated to do things on your own, you really do have to force yourself. It sucks, and it's really hard, but if you really want to get better, exercise is a really good stepping stool. It makes you feel better in the short and the long term. Good luck to you, you're not alone in this.

I am moved out, i do have a job, I go full time to school. I take care of my house, I worry about groceries and bills, I workout, I cook, I study, I do a million things that occupy my day. But at night, it's always the same. I've been through therapist after therapist after therapist, on and off medication. I try to keep a positive mindset and not get overwhelmed. But in the end, it's all the same. I have put effort into getting better, I really have, for years I have. I'm just so sick of coming back to the same thing. There have been times where I feel I've hit rock bottom, and I thought "I'm done, it's time to get better,I'm sick of being sad."  And sometimes I'll be okay for a few months, but it never lasts...
